Synopsis:
After the party, Astarion is standing in a corner, bottle of wine in hand, in a bad mood. Everything's too merry for him, not hedonistic enough. But there's the possibility of a little hedonism with the player, if you both agree to meet up for a little 'fun' later in the night. That's a tantilising thought - there might be something to look forward to after all.

Astarion is sulking in a corner with a bottle of wine — he finds the whole wholesome celebration grating and even complains that the wine tastes foul to him. He voices a desire for something more hedonistic and quietly propositions the player to meet later for private “fun.” This is a romance/party‑interaction moment: the player can tease, demand a courteous “please” (which flusters him), accept, or rebuff him, and Astarion’s response ranges from flirtatious compliance to annoyed withdrawal depending on choices and romance flags.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntRaiderCelebration_CRD_Astarion.json: Astarion is enjoying himself at a party with the goblins. He or you can propose that you get together tonight and enjoy a little more hedonism when everyone else is asleep.

For Astarion, this is a game of power - one he's played many times before in the taverns of Baldur's Gate, trying to lure people back to his master. He's an old hand at seduction, very self-assured at first, but the player might not go along with the script he expects them to follow. The next morning, the player wakes to see Astarion standing and getting dressed. They catch a glimpse of scars on his back - a sore point. The scars were carved into him by his old master. As far as Astarion knows, they're a poem, but he's never been able to read it (can't look in a mirror, after all).

context: The scene occurs at camp immediately after a raucous celebration for the goblin‑hunt — Astarion is standing apart with a bottle of wine, sulking because the wholesome toasts and good cheer grate on him. As a vampiric companion, wine tastes foul to him (in some variants he instead indulges in blood at the goblin festivities), and he voices a hunger for something more hedonistic than the party offers. Quietly, he propositions the player to meet later that night for private “fun,” treating seduction partly as a game of power he knows well. The player’s responses (teasing, demanding a courteous “please,” accepting, or rebuffing) will either fluster and flirt him or provoke annoyance and withdrawal.
